topic: Neonatal jaundice: assessment, phototherapy and exchange transfusion
scope: NICE CG98 recommendations on information, bilirubin thresholds, phototherapy, and exchange transfusion for babies under 28 days. Thresholds quoted here are the consensus table for babies of 38 weeks or more.

keyRecommendations.text: Use the consensus bilirubin thresholds. For babies 38 weeks or more, at 24 hours phototherapy starts above 200 micromol/L and exchange transfusion above 300 micromol/L.
During exchange transfusion do not stop continuous intensified phototherapy, do not perform a single-volume exchange, do not use albumin priming routinely, and do not give intravenous calcium.

Do not use agar, albumin, barbiturates, charcoal, cholestyramine, clofibrate, D-penicillamine, glycerin, manna, metalloporphyrins, riboflavin, traditional Chinese medicine, acupuncture, or homeopathy to treat hyperbilirubinaemia.

clinicalBottomLine: Interpret bilirubin against the gestational-age and hour-of-life threshold table, intensify phototherapy at the phototherapy threshold, and prepare exchange transfusion at the exchange threshold without stopping intensified phototherapy during the exchange.
notableCaveats: The AAP 2022 guideline suggested in the spreadsheet is not openly available as full text. CG98 is the open guideline used here. Thresholds differ by age in hours; the MCQs use only hours stated in the questions.

source.title: Jaundice in newborn babies under 28 days. NICE guideline CG98.
